## Overview

The repository has **1 commit**. `HEAD` and `--all` contain the same commit set.

## Key concepts

Canonical author identity:

- Corpus fixture `<fixture@example.invalid>`: 1 commit

## How it works

Primary evidence:

```sh
git rev-list --count HEAD       # 1
git rev-list --count --all      # 1
git log HEAD --format='%aN <%aE>' | sort | uniq -c
git log --all --format='%aN <%aE>' | sort | uniq -c
```

`%aN` and `%aE` use mailmap-resolved author names and emails.

These produced no output, proving neither set has unique commits:

```sh
git rev-list HEAD --not --all
git rev-list --all --not HEAD
```

`git shortlog -sne HEAD` and `git shortlog -sne --all` independently returned the same author and count. The sole commit is `d9722409cabd904e7339fda14fe1818d77be6641`.

## Gotchas

`--all` counts commits reachable from refs, not reflogs or unreachable objects. Only read-only commands ran, and `git status --short` remained empty.
